# Community Signal Scan

## Search Summary

## Opportunities

### VERIFIED OPPORTUNITY: Trial users leave before onboarding is complete

#### Conversation

- Community/source: Synthetic SaaS Founders Forum
- Title: Trial users leave before onboarding is complete
- URL: https://community.example.invalid/threads/trial-onboarding-dropoff
- Date: 2026-09-10

#### Problem Evidence

Observed first-person evidence: "I can see trial users start onboarding, but I cannot tell which step makes them leave before they reach their first useful result." The fictional author describes an early-stage SaaS context and uncertainty about where trial onboarding loses users.

#### Fit Assessment

- Audience fit: high — observed context says the author runs an early-stage SaaS company.
- Problem fit: high — the post directly describes inability to identify trial-user onboarding drop-off.
- Product fit: plausible — the fictional product context says it identifies onboarding drop-off steps; this is a fit inference, not evidence the author wants or will buy it.
- Confidence: medium — the synthetic post is accessible and specific, but one conversation does not establish broader demand.

#### Community Considerations

- Guidance: not evaluated in this offline synthetic case. Suitability for participation is unknown and must be checked by a human against current community guidance.

#### Helpful Response Draft

First, compare the steps completed by trial users who reach their first useful result with those who stop earlier; a simple step-by-step funnel can show where the largest drop occurs. If you can share which onboarding events you track, people may be able to suggest a useful breakdown.

A product mention is omitted because this fixture does not establish that the author wants a recommendation.

#### Review Status

Review Status: review

## Recurring Problems

No recurring pattern is established by one conversation.

## Recommended Experiment

A founder could manually compare one recent trial cohort by onboarding step and record where evidence is missing.

## Limitations

This is synthetic fixture output, not live research.
